newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, Zagrebacka hits new high.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, Zagrebacka hits new high.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed in slower trade on Wednesday, but traders predicted a continuation in the near future of the bullish trend set off by blue chips.
Five of 13 active issues rose, four fell and four were flat. Volume dipped to 8,194 shares from 12,074 on Tuesday and turnover was also lower at 5.5 million kuna.
"There is an excellent atmosphere surrounding the capital market," Damir Cikotic of Faktor brokerage told Reuters, referring to political stability after the latest elections.
"Pliva and Zagrebacka banka are definite bulls and they are the best thing that has happened to Croatian market," he added.
Zagrebacka's ordinaries climbed 22 kuna to hit 2,202.1 -- a new all-time high -- and sold 1,040 units. Its 1/10 GDRs earlier reached $37.685 on London's Seaq but have fallen since.
"Zagrebacka has got very good characteristics, but we cannot expect a big rise, because it has already achieved a very good price," said Ratko Bubalo of Eastbrokers.
He also recommended its preferred E-series: "We expect the price gap (between preferred and ordinary shares) to soon shrink to 50 from over 100 percent."
Fully-listed Pliva pharmaceuticals was the day's most active stock, adding 14 kuna to 474 on volume of 2,501 shares.
Its GDRs rose to $15.68 from Tuesday's $15.4 in London.
Brewery Karlovacka Pivovara led the day's gainers, climbing 25 kuna from last Friday to 290. But it only sold 161 shares.
The second most actively traded stock was food processor Podravka, stable at 305 kuna on volume of 2,161 units.
"I would recommend Podravka as one of the best long-term buys, same as (confectioner) Kras", said Bubalo.
Kras was also flat at 450 kuna with 760 shares sold.
Cikotic agreed Podravka would see significant growth in the autumn due to stronger demand when its shares are offered in exchange for vouchers under the mass privatisation scheme.
Three of four active hoteliers dipped on Wednesday, but traders foresaw the stocks coming to life with the summer's tourist season.
Biggest loser was hotelier Jadranturist, down 13 kuna to 290 trading 201 shares.
